skills.name: Upjohn
skills.description: Properly identifies representation and role with the Company, and that they cannot give the employee legal advice. This must always be part of the very beginning of the interview.
skills.reason: T2 says the interviewer represents the company, not the witness, but never says counsel cannot give the witness legal advice or states the purpose of the interview.

skills.name: Privilege
skills.description: Properly explains that the Company controls the privilege and determines how it is shared.
skills.reason: T2 explains that the privilege belongs to the company and that the company may decide to share what the witness says.

skills.name: Relationship
skills.description: Establishes rapport and interview expectations. This includes: establishes an appropriate professional tone; explains how the interview will proceed; encourages complete answers; instructs the witness that they can speculate, they just need to say when they do; invites the witness to distinguish between recollection and uncertainty.
skills.reason: Opens with a bare 'Good morning' and then moves straight into questions. It does not explain how the interview will proceed or tell the witness to flag speculation.

skills.name: Confirmation
skills.description: Checks the witness understood the Upjohn warning and answers their questions, if any.
skills.reason: T2 asks 'Any questions?' and the witness answers 'No. Go ahead.' The interviewer never checks that the witness understood the warning.

skills.name: Closing
skills.description: Closes by confirming there is "nothing else", next steps, a confidentiality reminder, and a reminder to keep records.
skills.reason: T80 asks whether anything else should be known, and T86 gives a confidentiality and document-retention reminder. There is no next-steps explanation and no instruction not to speak with other witnesses.

moments.text: I represent the company, not you. What we discuss is privileged, but the privilege belongs to the company, and the company may decide to share what you tell me. Any questions?
No. Go ahead.
Is there anything I haven't asked about that you think the Committee should know?
Please keep any related documents and keep this confidential. Thanks.

skills.name: Narrative Development
skills.description: Lets the witness walk through what happened.
skills.reason: Open prompts such as T10 and T16 let the witness explain LJM1 and the Board meeting in his own words (T11, T17).

skills.name: Funneling
skills.description: Moves in a sensible order from general to specific questions.
skills.reason: The interview moves from role (T4) to LJM1 (T10), then Chewco, LJM2, the Raptors and the personal interests, and then to the closing questions.

skills.name: Clarity
skills.description: Asks clear questions and avoids compound, ambiguous, or legalistic questions.
skills.reason: Several questions are leading or tag-style, such as T24 'wasn't it?', T68 'didn't you?' and T72 'So you were involved, weren't you?'.

skills.name: Professionalism
skills.description: Stays neutral, polite and in control.
skills.reason: The tone stays polite and controlled even when the interviewer confronts the witness with the Southampton and $10.5 million note contradictions (T58, T72).

skills.name: Adaptability
skills.description: Changes technique based on the witness's answers rather than staying only with the outline.
skills.reason: The interviewer changes course based on answers, for example asking how the witness knows what the Board was told (T34) and pressing on the Raptor returns after the vague answers (T47-T51).

moments.text: How did LJM1 come about in 1999?
Tell me about the June 28, 1999 Board meeting. What did you present?
How do you know Mr. Skilling told the Board?
So you were involved, weren't you?

areas.name: Fact Development, Source Identification, & Credibility Testing

skills.name: Ensures Credibility
skills.description: Recognizes and follows up on incomplete, evasive, or inconsistent answers.
skills.reason: The interviewer follows up on hearsay (T34-T35), on the Chewco buyout denial against the note (T72), and on the Southampton contradiction (T58).

skills.name: Material Facts
skills.description: Identifies the who, what, when, and how.
skills.reason: The interviewer establishes who suggested the GP role (T14), who decided the Southampton investment (T60), and when approvals were signed (T42).

skills.name: Memory Refreshing
skills.description: Tries other ways when the witness can't remember.
skills.reason: The note to 'Andy' is used to refresh memory (T72), but the approval sheets and investor reports the witness said he needed (T43, T51) were not put in front of him.

skills.name: Establishes Knowledge
skills.description: Separates what the witness personally knows from speculation, secondhand information, or inferences.
skills.reason: The interviewer separates first-hand knowledge from hearsay with 'How do you know Mr. Skilling told the Board?' (T34) and 'How do you know they reviewed every transaction?' (T38).

skills.name: Other Sources
skills.description: Identifies additional witnesses.
skills.reason: T82 asks who else to speak with, and the witness names Causey, Buy, Glisan, Kopper, Andersen and V&E, but the interviewer does not press further on any of them.

skills.name: Other Evidence
skills.description: Identifies other documents such as communications, reports, notes, or other relevant records.
skills.reason: T84 asks what documents to review, and the witness identifies the approval sheets and partnership agreements, but the interviewer does not pursue the communications or the handwritten memo.

skills.name: Tests Certainty
skills.description: Examines how certain the witness is about their memory or a fact.
skills.reason: The interviewer tests certainty on the Board's understanding (T34-T35) and on the review process (T38-T39), but lets 'I don't recall' (T73, T77) and 'I may have had a call' (T79) pass untested.

skills.name: Follow-Up
skills.description: Recognizes material responses and follows up on them.
skills.reason: The interviewer follows up well on most answers, but at T43 the witness admits some approvals were papered after closing and the interviewer moves on without asking which deals.

moments.text: How do you know they reviewed every transaction?
When did they sign it, relative to the closing?
Some approvals were papered after a deal closed. That happened.
Who else should we speak with to understand these transactions?

skills.name: Effective Selection
skills.description: Selects and contextualizes documents effectively, and properly authenticates the document.
skills.reason: The Southampton agreement and the note are identified (T58, T72), but neither is authenticated or shown in a way that places it in context for the witness.

skills.name: Narrative
skills.description: Gets the witness's story first, before using conflicting evidence.
skills.reason: The witness is asked about the Foundation's investments (T52-T57) before the Southampton document is raised at T58, and about the buyout (T70) before the note is put to him at T72.

skills.name: Accuracy
skills.description: Describes the document accurately.
skills.reason: The interviewer's descriptions match the record: the $25,000 foundation contribution, about $4.5 million received about six weeks later, and the $10.5 million figure in the note.

skills.name: Avoid Initial Conclusion
skills.description: Separates the document from inferences or conclusions, unless the witness takes an unreasonable stance.
skills.reason: The interviewer states conclusions before letting the witness explain, such as 'Isn't that inconsistent with what you told the Board?' (T58) and 'So you were involved, weren't you?' (T72).

skills.name: Fairness
skills.description: Provides the witness with a fair opportunity to explain any inconsistencies or disagreements with the document.
skills.reason: The witness gets a chance to explain the Southampton and note inconsistencies (T59, T73), and his explanations are recorded in full.

moments.text: This is the Southampton Place partnership agreement. It shows a $25,000 contribution from your family foundation, and our information is the foundation received about $4.5 million about six weeks later. Isn't that inconsistent with what you told the Board?
This note to "Andy" mentions $10.5 million for the buyout. So you were involved, weren't you?
The Foundation isn't me, and what I told the Board was about my economics as general partner. This was a separate investment, made later, on market terms.

missed_opportunities: T43: The witness says some approvals were papered after closing. The interviewer moves on to the Raptor returns without asking which deals were affected or how the witness knows.

T77: On the $2.6 million tax indemnity payment the witness says 'I don't recall authorizing it' and points to the business unit and legal. The interviewer does not put to him the events-log account that he told counsel Skilling had decided the payment should be made.
tips: When you say some approvals were papered after a deal closed, which specific deals were they, how do you know that happened, and who else would know?
Before showing the Southampton agreement, what did you understand the Foundation's role to be, where did its $25,000 come from, and what did you know about the other Enron employees who invested?
